relevance_note: A review with four illustrative adult cases, three with printed GFAP variants, e.g. "GFAP gene analysis identified a heterozygous c.250 G>A p.Arg79His missense variant".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON from values I wrote, then checked spans and fields. Labels: the paper uses 'Case N' in headings and 'case N' in figure captions about equally; 'Case 1'..'Case 4' used throughout. Case 4 is included as in scope because the authors present him among their adult AxD cases ('He was suspected to have possible adult-onset AxD'; figure 6 'changes consistent with AxD'), but the paper reports no GFAP variant or genetic result for him, so he has no variants row. Case 1's disease label is left 'not reported' because no sentence names his diagnosis (heading says only 'ataxic presentation'). Not given rows: Case 1's 'two close relatives' with reported multiple sclerosis (no individual-level detail, not described as having AxD or a GFAP variant) and Case 2's mother (informant only). Case 2's mother's concern that the patient 'might have had an unsteady gait and intellectual disability' is hedged and was not recorded as observed; developmental delay and ataxia stay 'not reported' for Case 2. Case 2's earlier diagnosis of spinocerebellar degeneration is a misdiagnosis and not recorded as a feature. Case 1 'no bulbar features' was taken to exclude the narrower checklist items dysphagia and dysarthria; 'no sphincter problems' does not exclude the composite autonomic item (orthostatic hypotension, sleep apnea not addressed); 'full range of eye movements' was not taken to exclude the composite eye movement item. Periventricular abnormalities and frontal-horn capping lesions were recorded as cerebral white matter abnormality, not as 'periventricular rim'. Age at onset: Case 2 'late 30s' is her first presentation (repeated falls), although febrile convulsions in infancy were reported later; Case 1 and 4 onset taken from first presentation ('early 40s', 'early 50s'); decade ranges were not converted to ISO 8601. study_type from the authors' footnote 'This literature review'; the cases come from the authors' review of patient records. Variant reference ^20 is a variant database (Waisman Center), not a prior report of these patients. Case 3 protein string printed as 'pSer247Phe' (no period) and recorded as printed. Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27): normal facial expression, full eye movement range, normal left-side strength, normal sensation, normal patellar reflexes, preservation of the pons. No contradictions found. No tables describe individuals (Tables 1-2 are general).
